title: Tactile guidance improved immediate racket-skill ratings in a randomized study
summary: After ten minutes of practice, 12 learners given contact and motion guidance improved by 0.72 levels on a four-level expert rating scale. Twelve learners who received only proficiency-level feedback gained 0.05 levels. The difference was 0.67 levels (95% confidence interval 0.39 to 0.98).
ai_technology: GNN–LSTM pose estimator; graph-informed drive–grip encoder and decoder
organization: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

source_review.scope: Front matter; hand–racket reconstruction, control organization, mechanism-guided learning, and Supplementary Notes 14–16

evidence.tested: A separate cohort of 24 was randomly assigned to equal-duration practice. Three experts rated shuffled before-and-after clips without labels identifying the group or assessment time.
evidence.unknown: This small study evaluated immediate changes on five racket skills. Durability and transfer to match play were unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: A learned pose estimator reconstructed contact geometry from tactile input. Learned control representations and regional analysis informed feedback on how each learner’s contact and timing differed from an expert reference.
